problem: Existing RAG (naive, GraphRAG, LightRAG) and robot maps (metric, semantic, 3D scene graphs) cannot make large, redundant, multimodal embodied experience searchable at multiple abstraction levels. Text-chunk RAG fails to retrieve the correct images or poses, and graph RAG is slow to build.
motivation: Robots accumulate unbounded experience that must be searchable and actionable for queries ranging from an object ("find a bench") to an ambiance or a global description. Embodied data is spatially correlated and redundant, so semantic similarity alone confuses the retriever, and scene graphs need hand-made schemas that do not transfer to outdoor spaces.
key_idea: Cluster a topological map of captioned poses into a hierarchical semantic forest by spatial plus semantic distance, summarize each level with an LLM, and retrieve with LLM-guided top-down parallel tree traversal plus spatial/sensor re-ranking.
insight: Retrieval reasoning over the hierarchy matters more than similarity search. In the ablation, baselines retrieving from Embodied-RAG's own memory match its P(Q|A) but produce longer paths, so it wins on P(Q|A,L) through the spatial re-ranking. Spatial clustering also cuts LLM calls, giving 7.38x faster building than GraphRAG, and extra sensor data (NDVI) improves only Embodied-RAG.
method: Topological map: nodes hold pose (x,y,z,yaw), timestamp, ego image and a GPT-4o caption, connected by path history or a distance threshold, independent of the robot's embodiment

Semantic forest: complete-linkage hierarchical clustering with hybrid similarity S=(1-α)·spatial(haversine exponential decay)+α·semantic(cosine of text embeddings), then LLM summaries per cluster form higher-level nodes until roots
Top-down retrieval phase 1: an LLM selection function f_LLM(q, C_l, k) picks the top-k child nodes per level, run as parallel tree traversals inspired by Tree-of-Thoughts, down to leaf nodes

Retrieval phase 2, hybrid re-ranking: an LLM scores the leaves and duplicates are removed; if the agent location L is given, spatial-proximity scores are mixed in; other sensors (NDVI grass quality) can be added to the score

Generation: an LLM outputs a JSON waypoint with reasoning for find queries, or text for explain queries; Dijkstra on the topological graph gives the global path, and a local planner (Unitree Go2 go-to-waypoint) executes it

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (captioning, selection, generation), GPT-4 summarizer (frozen, prompted)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB images with poses and timestamps (topological graph), optionally NDVI sensor data
setting.action_space: waypoints on topological graph, Dijkstra global path, local planner via Unitree Go2 go-to-waypoint API
setting.simulator: AirSim (14 simulated environments), plus real robots and Google Street View data
setting.privileged: perfect local planner assumed; ground-truth topological graph with poses given; queries known to annotators

numbers_note: Custom benchmark only, with no standard navigation benchmarks. Evaluation uses VLM-voted probabilities, not SR. Table IV (ablation with shared memory, Top-1/Top-5) is not listed.
results: Embodied-RAG far exceeds Naive-RAG, GraphRAG and LightRAG on explicit and implicit find queries (e.g. P(Q|A) 0.55 vs 0.08 on explicit E-image). It matches the graph baselines on global queries, with SS 0.67 vs 0.68 for GraphRAG on E-image, and reaches 0.95 with sensor data. It builds memory 7.38x faster than GraphRAG and 9.76x faster than LightRAG, about 4 min 35 s for 3,353 nodes.
limitations: Assumes a perfect local planner and static environments; dynamic objects and stale observations are not handled
Fails at fine-grained counting and multi-view consistency
Depends on (V)LM APIs and thus internet access; the queries and dataset are small and self-made (about 250 queries)
